question_text: Find the value of the unknown:

mark_breakdown.desc: Recognize angle in a semicircle is a right angle

subparts.solution: $A\hat{C}B = 90^\circ$ {angle in a semi-circle}, so $\triangle ABC$ is right angled at $C$. Since the radius is $5\text{ cm}$, the diameter is $AB = 10\text{ cm}$. $\cos\theta = \frac{7}{AB} = \frac{7}{10} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{10}\right) \approx 45.6^\circ$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Thales's theorem: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle ($90^\circ$).
step_by_step: Recognize that $\triangle ABC$ is a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse equal to the diameter $2 \times 5 = 10\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the radius $5\text{ cm}$ as the hypotenuse instead of the diameter $10\text{ cm}$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Use tangent-radius property to identify right angle

subparts.solution: We construct the right angled triangle as shown. For the shaded triangle, $\tan 18^\circ = \frac{20}{x} \implies x = \frac{20}{\tan 18^\circ} \approx 61.6$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
step_by_step: Identify that the radius of $20\text{ m}$ is perpendicular to the tangent line.
In the resulting right triangle, set up $\tan 18^\circ = \frac{20}{x}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing sine and tangent when dealing with tangent lines to circles.

mark_breakdown.desc: Construct altitude to split chord and apex angle

subparts.solution: We construct the altitude as shown. For the shaded triangle, $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{3}{4} \implies \frac{\theta}{2} = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) \implies \theta = 2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) \approx 97.2^\circ$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord and the central angle.
step_by_step: The chord of length $6\text{ m}$ is bisected into two segments of $3\text{ m}$.
The radius of $4\text{ m}$ serves as the hypotenuse.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using $6$ instead of $3$ as the opposite side length.
